title: Install NVIDIA drivers
description: Guided, checked installation of the right NVIDIA driver for your graphics card.
author: Tux Store

welcome.title: Before you install
message: Before installing, make sure your system is fully updated.
This guide will check your computer, help you pick the right NVIDIA driver and install it. A restart is needed at the end.

no_yay.title: yay is missing
message: Install yay first.
yay is needed to install the older driver versions from the AUR. Once it is installed, open this guide again.

command.label: Checking your system…
shell: [ "$(id -u)" -ne 0 ] || { echo "Tux Store is running as root. yay refuses to build packages as root, so start Tux Store as a normal user."; exit 0; }
for t in lspci pkexec script curl pacman; do
command -v "$t" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "The required tool '$t' is missing (lspci comes from the 'pciutils' package)."; exit 0; }
[ ! -e /var/lib/pacman/db.lck ] || { echo "pacman is locked (/var/lib/pacman/db.lck exists). Another package manager may be running. Wait for it to finish, then try again."; exit 0; }

[ -d "/usr/lib/modules/$(uname -r)" ] || { echo "The kernel you are running ($(uname -r)) was replaced by an update and its modules are gone. Restart your computer first, then run this again."; exit 0; }
[ "${avail:-0}" -ge 4194304 ] || { echo "Less than 4 GiB of free space on /. Free some space first: building a kernel module needs room."; exit 0; }

[ "$n" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$n package update(s) are waiting. Update your system first (Updates tab), restart if the kernel was updated, then run this again. Installing drivers on a half-updated system can break the graphics stack."; exit 0; }
curl -fsI --max-time 10 https://archlinux.org >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "No internet connection (archlinux.org is unreachable)."; exit 0; }

command.label: Looking for your graphics card…
shell: # The PCI id database does not know this chip name: fall back to the marketing name.

command.label: Checking your kernels…
shell: # One "<pkgbase>-headers" per installed kernel (pkgbase comes from the kernel package itself).
[ -n "$pk" ] || { echo "No installed kernel package was found."; exit 2; }
case "$b" in *[!a-z0-9@._+-]*) echo "Unexpected kernel package name: $b"; exit 4 ;; esac

[ -z "$miss" ] || { echo "No headers package could be found for the kernel(s):$miss. The NVIDIA module cannot be built for them. Install their headers (or use the official linux / linux-lts kernels) and try again."; exit 3; }

no_gpu.title: No NVIDIA graphics card found
message: I could not find an NVIDIA graphics card on this computer.

On a laptop with hybrid graphics that is dual-booted with Windows, power-saving modes (for example ASUS “Eco Mode”) can switch the NVIDIA GPU off at firmware level so Linux cannot see it. Switch Windows or the BIOS to Standard / Optimized mode, shut down completely, and boot Arch again.
If you are sure a card is installed (for example you are preparing a disk for another PC), you can continue anyway.

choose_driver.title: Choose the driver
choose_driver.message:
Detected graphics card: ${gpu_model}

Pick the driver branch. The one marked “Recommended” matches your card.

options.label: NVIDIA drivers — latest
options.hint:
The newest official NVIDIA driver (open kernel modules). This is the latest version of the NVIDIA drivers. For GeForce RTX 20/30/40/50 and GTX 16 series (Turing and newer). From the official Arch repositories.
Note: a few RTX 30 laptops freeze with this driver; if that happens, use 580.xx instead.

notes.text: ⚠ Your GPU (${gpu_model}) looks like it needs a different driver.

options.label: NVIDIA drivers 580.xx
options.hint: For GeForce GTX 10 (Pascal), GTX 9 / GTX 750 (Maxwell) and Volta. These cards are no longer supported by the latest driver. Installed from the AUR.

notes.text: ⚠ Your GPU (${gpu_model}) looks like it needs a different driver.

set.driver_source: the AUR (community packages, built on your computer)

options.label: NVIDIA drivers 470.xx
options.hint: For GeForce 600 / 700 series (Kepler). Legacy: NVIDIA no longer updates it. Installed from the AUR.

notes.text: ⚠ Your GPU (${gpu_model}) looks like it needs a different driver.

set.driver_source: the AUR (community packages, built on your computer)
set.driver_warning: This driver is no longer maintained by NVIDIA. It may fail to build against the newest kernel (the linux-lts kernel is the safer choice), and on Intel 11th gen or newer CPUs it may need the kernel parameter ibt=off to boot.

options.label: NVIDIA drivers 390.xx
options.hint: For GeForce 400 / 500 series (Fermi). Legacy and unsupported. Installed from the AUR.

notes.text: ⚠ Your GPU (${gpu_model}) looks like it needs a different driver.

set.driver_source: the AUR (community packages, built on your computer)
set.driver_warning: This driver is no longer maintained by NVIDIA and may fail to build against new kernels or Xorg versions. If it does, the open-source nouveau driver is the fallback.

options.label: NVIDIA drivers 340.xx
options.hint: For GeForce 8 / 9 / 200 / 300 series (Tesla). Very old, legacy and unsupported. Installed from the AUR.

notes.text: ⚠ Your GPU (${gpu_model}) looks like it needs a different driver.

set.driver_source: the AUR (community packages, built on your computer)
set.driver_warning: This driver is very old and unsupported. It will most likely fail on recent kernels and Xorg versions. Consider the open-source nouveau driver instead.

mismatch.title: This driver may not fit your card
message: Your graphics card (${gpu_model}) belongs to the “${gpu_branch}” driver family, but you chose “${driver}”.
A driver that does not support your card can leave you with a black screen after the restart.

confirm.title: Are you sure?
message: You are about to install:
${driver_label}
Source: ${driver_source}
Kernel headers for: ${headers}
Existing NVIDIA driver packages that conflict will be replaced. You will need to restart the computer afterwards.
${driver_warning}
Do you want to continue?

install_headers.title: Preparing…
install_headers.message: Please don't turn off the computer until I'm finished.

commands.label: Installing build tools and kernel headers

install_driver.title: Installing the driver…
install_driver.message: Please don't turn off the computer until I'm finished.

commands.label: Installing ${driver_label}
shell: if pacman -Sl multilib >/dev/null 2>&1; then L32="lib32-nvidia-utils"; fi
# --ask 4: let pacman replace conflicting NVIDIA packages inside ONE transaction,
# so the system is never left without a driver in between.

commands.label: Installing ${driver_label}
shell: case "$B" in 580xx|470xx|390xx|340xx) ;; *) echo "Unexpected driver branch: $B"; exit 2 ;; esac
if pacman -Sl multilib >/dev/null 2>&1; then L32="lib32-nvidia-$B-utils"; fi
# yay must run as a normal user; --sudo pkexec makes it ask for the password in a graphical dialog.

commands.label: Rebuilding the boot images
shell: if command -v mkinitcpio >/dev/null 2>&1; then mkinitcpio -P; else echo "mkinitcpio not found (dracut or another tool?): skipping."; fi

command.label: Verifying the driver was built…
shell: # Every installed kernel must now have an NVIDIA module (DKMS can fail without failing pacman).
[ -z "$bad" ] || { echo "The NVIDIA kernel module was NOT built for:$bad"; exit 1; }

verify_failed.title: The driver was not built correctly
message: ${verify_msg}
Do NOT restart yet. Use “Show details” to read what went wrong. The kernel headers may not match the kernel, or the build failed.

shell: echo "Optional: your /etc/mkinitcpio.conf HOOKS contains 'kms'. Removing it keeps nouveau out of the initramfs (then run: sudo mkinitcpio -P)."

done_modern.title: Driver installed
message: The driver was installed successfully. Please restart the computer.
${kms_text}

done_legacy.title: Driver installed
message: The driver was installed successfully. Please restart the computer.

If you use Wayland: this older driver needs the kernel parameter nvidia_drm.modeset=1 nvidia_drm.fbdev=1 in your bootloader (for GRUB: GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT in /etc/default/grub, then regenerate the config). Add it BEFORE you restart, otherwise Wayland may show a black screen.
${kms_text}

install_failed.title: The installation did not finish
message: Something went wrong while installing (step: ${last_failed}). Use “Show details” to read the output.

pacman works in all-or-nothing transactions, so your old driver is normally still in place. If the cause is a conflict with an older NVIDIA package, I can remove the NVIDIA driver packages and try again — but you would have no NVIDIA driver until the new one is installed.

buttons.label: Remove old NVIDIA packages and retry

confirm_cleanup.title: Remove the NVIDIA driver packages?
message: All installed NVIDIA driver packages will be removed, then ${driver_label} will be installed again.
Do not turn off or restart the computer until it is finished.

cleanup.title: Removing old packages…
cleanup.message: Please don't turn off the computer until I'm finished.

commands.label: Removing old NVIDIA packages
shell: if [ -z "$pk" ]; then echo "No NVIDIA driver packages are installed."; exit 0; fi
# -Rdd: other packages depend on these (steam, egl-wayland…); the replacement is installed right after.

error_generic.title: A check failed
message: “${last_failed}” did not work (exit code ${last_exit_code}).
${last_output}

command.label: Reading the installed version…
shell: case "$TUX_VAR_DRIVER" in open) p=nvidia-utils ;; *) p="nvidia-$TUX_VAR_DRIVER-utils" ;; esac

un_confirm.title: Remove the NVIDIA driver?
message: This removes: ${recorded_packages}
Afterwards the computer uses the open-source nouveau driver. If the screen stays black after the restart, switch to a text console (Ctrl+Alt+F3) and reinstall from there.
Do not turn off the computer while it is working.

command.label: Checking your system…
shell: command -v pkexec >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "The required tool 'pkexec' is missing."; exit 0; }
[ ! -e /var/lib/pacman/db.lck ] || { echo "pacman is locked (/var/lib/pacman/db.lck exists). Another package manager may be running."; exit 0; }

un_run.title: Removing the driver…
un_run.message: Please don't turn off the computer until I'm finished.

commands.label: Removing the NVIDIA packages
shell: if [ -z "$inst" ]; then echo "None of the recorded packages are installed any more."; exit 0; fi

commands.label: Rebuilding the boot images
shell: if command -v mkinitcpio >/dev/null 2>&1; then mkinitcpio -P; else echo "mkinitcpio not found: skipping."; fi

un_done.title: Driver removed
un_done.message: The NVIDIA driver was removed. Please restart the computer.

un_failed.title: The driver could not be removed
message: Step: ${last_failed}. Use “Show details” to read the output.
Other programs may depend on one of these packages (for example Steam needs the 32-bit libraries). The driver is still installed, and so is its record, so you can try again later.

download_mb.label: Download size
shell: pacman -Si nvidia-open-dkms nvidia-utils nvidia-settings 2>/dev/null | awk '/^Download Size/ {v=$4; u=$5; if (u=="KiB") v/=1024; else if (u=="GiB") v*=1024; else if (u=="B") v/=1048576; t+=v} END {printf "%d\n", t+0.5}'

installed_mb.label: Installed size
shell: pacman -Si nvidia-open-dkms nvidia-utils nvidia-settings 2>/dev/null | awk '/^Installed Size/ {v=$4; u=$5; if (u=="KiB") v/=1024; else if (u=="GiB") v*=1024; else if (u=="B") v/=1048576; t+=v} END {printf "%d\n", t+0.5}'

info.note: Download and installed sizes are read from your package database for the latest driver. Older drivers from the AUR are built on your computer (about 350 MB download); the space needed while installing is an estimate.
